utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case IT‑96‑21‑I, the Prosecutor against Zdravko Mucic.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Can everyone hear me, everyone who is using a microphone? Can everyone hear me in the language they understand? Mr. Mucic? Very good. OK. This is an initial appearance pursuant to Rule 62 of the Tribunal's Rules of Procedure and Evidence. May I have the appearances for the Prosecutor, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: I am Eric Ostberg, senior trial attorney and I appear today with my co‑counsel, Mrs. Teresa McHenry.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you. May I have the appearances for the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. RHODES
utterances.text: May it please your Honour, Robert Rhodes, Queen's Counsel, assigned counsel for Mr. Mucic.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Rhodes, remember to use the microphone. Thank you so much. Are there any additional appearances? Is the Prosecutor ready to proceed with the initial appearance?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour, but before that I have a correction to make in the indictment. On page 6 of the indictment in the English version, at least, there is a misprint, if I can ‑‑‑

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: In the English version?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: ‑‑ take you to paragraph 22? Paragraph 22, page 6, in the middle of that paragraph, seven or eight lines from the bottom, it reads ,"and including all the murders described above in paragraph 17 to 22", should be "16 to 21". The same misprint appears in the Serbo Croatian translation; in the French translation, however, it is correctly put. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Rhodes, did you follow that request? It would be paragraph 22 of the indictment in the English version and in the Serbo Croatian version they would be changed. It is the French version that is correct. I do not suppose you have read all versions, have you?

utterances.speaker: MR. RHODES
utterances.text: No, your Honour, not yet. Mr. Ostberg was kind enough to inform me before your Honour came into court that he would be applying to make this amendment; of course, it does not take me by surprise or prejudice me in any way.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Very good, thank you. Then leave will be granted to the Prosecutor to submit the corrected version, that is, just correcting this typographical error in the English and in the Serbo Croatian version. Mr. Rhodes, is the Defence ready to proceed?

utterances.speaker: MR. RHODES
utterances.text: Only ready to proceed with this hearing, but not any further.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Fine, thank you. Mr. Rhodes, has Mr. Mucic received a copy of the indictment?

utterances.speaker: MR. RHODES
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Has he read it or has he had it read to him in a language he understands?

utterances.speaker: MR. RHODES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Have you had an opportunity to discuss with Mr. Mucic the indictment?

utterances.speaker: MR. RHODES
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes. Pleas of not guilty are entered by Mr. Mucic in respect of all these charges.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: In your opinion, does Mr. Mucic ‑‑ I have a few more questions to ask you; actually, if you take a look at our Rule 62 of our Rules of Procedure and Evidence, they require a lot of us, so I am kind of going through this, if I may ‑‑ understand the nature of the charges against him contained in the indictment?

utterances.speaker: MR. RHODES
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is Mr. Mucic ready to proceed with a reading of the indictment for the purposes of an entry of a plea or does he wish to waive the reading of the indictment in its entirety?

utterances.speaker: MR. RHODES
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have not had an opportunity of asking him that specific thing. Might I just approach my client?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes, you may.

utterances.speaker: MR. RHODES
utterances.text: Your Honour, it is not necessary for the indictment to be read.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Mucic, would you please stand? Would you please stand, sir? Are you ready to proceed with an entry of a plea to the counts in the indictment in which you are charged?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: For the record, sir, would you state your full name?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MUCIC
utterances.text: My name is Zdravko Mucic.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Have you ever been known by a nickname?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MUCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: And what is that nickname, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MUCIC
utterances.text: "Pavo", that is my nickname, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Ostberg, would you identify the counts in the indictment to which you wish Mr. Mucic to enter a plea?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Yes. These are the following counts, 13 and 14, 33 to 35, 38 to 39, 44 to including 49. That would be the counts pertaining to Mr. Mucic.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Mucic, you have received a copy of the indictment, have you not?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MUCIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Are you ready to enter a plea with respect to these counts of the indictment?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MUCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: How do you plead, guilty or not guilty as to count 13 of the indictment?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MUCIC
utterances.text: I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: As to count 14 of the indictment, how do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MUCIC
utterances.text: Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: As to count 33 of the indictment, how do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MUCIC
utterances.text: Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: As to count 34 of the indictment, how do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MUCIC
utterances.text: Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: As to count 35 of the indictment, how do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MUCIC
utterances.text: Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: As to count 38 of the indictment, how do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MUCIC
utterances.text: Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: As to count 39 of the indictment, how do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MUCIC
utterances.text: Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: As to counts 44 through and including count 49, how do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MUCIC
utterances.text: Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Fine, thank you. You may be seated. Mr. Ostberg, have I called out all of the counts to which you wish Mr. Mucic to enter a plea?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Yes, you have, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Are there any preliminary matters that need to be addressed by counsel at this time? Mr. Ostberg?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: No, we have nothing special for the moment.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Rhodes?

utterances.speaker: MR. RHODES
utterances.text: Not at the moment, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is the Prosecutor ready to proceed to trial?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: And Mr. Rhodes, are you ready to proceed to trial?

utterances.speaker: MR. RHODES
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Once again, Mr. Rhodes, Rule 62 of our Rules of Procedure and Evidence suggest that I should set a date for trial which I will endeavour to do after we talk a little bit. Do you intend on filing any preliminary motions, Mr. Rhodes? Rule 73 of our Rules provides for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RHODES
utterances.text: Your Honour, it is too early to say; I have only received instructions in this case within the last 48 hours. I have still to receive the Prosecution witness statements and other material.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: As I have indicated, you have 60 days to file any preliminary motions. Rule 66, Mr. Ostberg, provides that the Prosecutor shall make available to the Defence as soon as practicable after the initial appearance of the accused, copies of the supporting material which accompanied the indictment when confirmation was sought, as well as all prior statements obtained by the Prosecutor from the accused or from Prosecution witnesses. When do you think you will provide that information to Mr. Rhodes?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: We will be able to do that in the following week. We have to do some redacting of the indictment from the point of view of protecting the victims, chiefly the rape victims. We will do that tomorrow and the beginning of next week, and I think during the next week, at the latest next Friday, we would be able to provide the Defence with supporting material.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Then by April 19th, that is the Friday of next week, you will provide; is that sufficient time?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Rhodes, the Prosecutor will provide you with that material called for in the Rule by April 19th.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: May I, your Honour, raise some issues, not exactly a motion but some comments?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: The indictment encompasses, as you see from the heading of it, another three indicted persons, more than Mr. Mucic. One of them, by the name of Zejnil Delalic, has been arrested in Germany. We do not know now exactly when he will be delivered or transferred to the Tribunal, maybe in a couple of weeks, maybe even next week; we are not certain yet, but he is arrested in Munich of Germany. It is material to this trial that the case against Mr. Mucic and Mr. Delalic be tried in one piece, that we try them together. Therefore, your Honour, I suggest that the date for the trial not be set until Delalic has arrived in The Hague and we know what kind of motions he will make and what we can do. It is premature, I think, today to set a trial date. I think we would find a date, your Honour, for a status conference to discuss this question some time after the arrival of Mr. Delalic.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Rhodes, do you have a comment to make with respect to that suggestion?

utterances.speaker: MR. RHODES
utterances.text: Simply that it seems a very sensible suggestion to be made.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I do not know that Mr. Mucic should really wait for another individual. I do not know when that other individual may be arriving, if he will be.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. If there is some delay more than, say, two or three weeks, then, of course, we cannot wait but for a reasonable period of time, I think it is a good thing to do so.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: By April 19th the Prosecutor will provide the Defence with the accompanied material. We will set a status conference with the Chamber. The Prosecutor and the Defence should appear at the status conference on May 14th 1996 at 9 a.m. That will enable the Chamber to assess the progress of the case in terms of the additional defendant as well as Mr. Rhodes to hear from you with respect to any preliminary motions that you may file. After the status conference on May 14th, we will set a date for the trial. Is that acceptable?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Are there any additional matters that need to be brought to the attention of the Chamber at this time?

utterances.speaker: MR. RHODES
utterances.text: Not on my behalf, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Ostberg?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Nor on mine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SIDHWA
utterances.text: Mr. Rhodes, you can also file any applications for motions even before 14th May, if you want to.

utterances.speaker: MR. RHODES
utterances.text: I am obliged, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SIDHWA
utterances.text: You are not obliged to wait to the 14th.

utterances.speaker: MR. RHODES
utterances.text: I am obliged, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there anything else, Mr. Ostberg?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Rhodes? And you understand what Judge Sidhwa is saying, that if you want to you can file a motion just as soon as you wish but you do have 60 days which is the outside limit. So take a look at the Rules. Thank you very much. We stand adjourned.
